app: 1. Habit Tracker - Goal Tracker & ADHD Planner
text:
Life-changing tool for building consistent habits — Habit Tracker has made a huge positive impact on my daily routine. As a student and cybersecurity researcher, I always struggled with staying consistent, but this app changed that. The GitHub-style contribution stack view is especially motivating—it gives me a clear picture of my progress and pushes me to keep going every day.

I love how simple yet powerful the design is. It’s fully customizable, easy to use, and helps me stay on top of my goals without feeling overwhelmed. Within just a short time, I’ve been able to build healthier habits and manage my time more effectively.

This app has genuinely made my life more organized, productive, and balanced. I highly recommend it to anyone who wants to stay consistent, achieve their goals, and track progress in a visually satisfying way.

app: 1. Habit Tracker - Goal Tracker & ADHD Planner
text: GitHub-Style Year View is a Game Changer — The year-view is game changer. Unlike most habit apps that only show recent week, or at best a month, this app lets you see your entire year in one view. If you use GiHub, you know how motivating it is to see this scope of time. Tracking your habits over the course of a year is the appropriate scope because habits often don’t “kick-in” or matter for almost close to a year. Having a year-long target means you’re getting a realistic understanding of the effect of a habit and not just a short snapshot, which doesn’t inform you much about the story of long-term positive change. Habits are fully customizable with frequency, weekly targets, color, name, icon, reminders, duration, units to measure (minutes, hours, miles, kilometers). You can even create your own units! Want to do 100 backflips per day , three days per weeks between Monday - Friday at 11:30AM!? You can do that with this app! This app has, is, and will continue to change my life. Download it now!

text: Great app! — Habit Tracker seems to excel in providing a seamless user experience with its Interactive Widgets, allowing users to manage daily progress conveniently from the Home Screen. The inclusion of detailed statistics, including daily progress, streaks, and a heatmap for the current year, provides valuable insights into habit performance. The integration with iOS 17 features such as Shortcuts and Spotlight enhances accessibility and usability. Additionally, the motivational phrases sourced from popular habit books like "Atomic Habits" add an extra layer of encouragement for users. With its focus on simplicity and essential features, Habit Tracker appears to be a valuable tool for anyone striving to build and maintain positive habits.

app: 1. Habit Tracker - Goal Tracker & ADHD Planner
text:
Handy, minimalistic habit tracker — Coming from Android, I was looking for an alternative to Habit Now. This app was exactly what I was looking for! 

I love the sort of “heat map” that gives a quick glance as to how I performed with my habits on any particular day, plus the general reports to see changes over time. 

But my favourite feature is the memos which I find are extremely useful for writing down notes related to the accomplishment of a habit on a given day. I love being able to look back to verify something I’ve done or didn’t do. 

Having the neat widget on screen also motivates me to keep track of my habits so it’s a win all around. 

Thanks so much for this great app!

app: 1. Habit Tracker - Goal Tracker & ADHD Planner
text: Great start — Been using this a couple days and seems to cover most all the options I was looking for in one place. Especially like the timers and counters built into the habit itself. I wish it would sync with FitBit app for steps and exercise (I don’t use the Health app) but that’s not a big deal. The charts are great to see the streaks in real time and a very non-judgemental way to evaluate myself without having to transfer data or color in boxes myself. Thanks!

app: 1. Habit Tracker - Goal Tracker & ADHD Planner
text: Good Visuals — I’m enjoying this Habit Tracker over some of the other ones available because (in my opinion) it has more pleasing visual trackers. I especially like the function that lights up little boxes to show you how often you’ve done that habit during the entire year.
Beatiful — This is the only app that made me setup a billing account so I can use the premium features. It works flawlessly. The ui is excellent and the dev updates it continuously. 10/10

Simple, elegante y potente — La app es fantástica, desde un punto de vista de UX está muy bien diseñada, es simple pero poderosa. Estoy usándola para micro hábitos, me gusta la forma en que visualmente se representan las rachas, pagué la versión pro y esta siendo la mejor compra del año hasta ahora

Der beste Habit Tracker! — Habe mindestens 5 verschiedene Habit Tracker probiert, HabitKit ist mit Abstand der Beste! 
Die Möglichkeit anhand des Rasters auf einem Blick alles zu sehen ist nicht nur motivierend sondern auch unglaublich hilfreich um bestimmte Muster in der Vergangenheit zu erkennen!

Falls es irgendwann auch noch möglich sein sollte eine mehrzeilige Beschreibung für jedes Habit in der Overview anzuzeigen (für die persönliche Motivation) wäre das der Oberhammer!!

Danke an den Entwickler für diese großartige App!!!
Beste Habit Tracker App — Das Design ist so simple und schön. Ich mag, dass es mich ein wenig an GitHub erinnert. Man ist richtig motiviert alle Kacheln auszufüllen
Love the simplicity — The app makes it super easy and fast to track your everyday habits. Love that you get a overview about your progress right away with the visualisation as dots!

Loving this with a little thought — Used this since start of 2025 and have been loving it! Thankfully have formed few habits thanks to the data visualization that gives a satisfying nudge regularly.
Wanting to make a suggested add-on feature, which is allowing people to log thoughts on dot when they completed a habit task, would be a great record keeping journal.
Subscription locked — Looks like it could be a great app. But expecting a yearly fee just to have widget. Ridiculous

Works well! — It does what it says on the tin. Intuitive and allows for broad customisation. Would be nice if there were more colours or some kind of colour swatch picker thing. Only real gripe is the quite restrictive number of habits available without premium, but I guess you get what you pay for. It didn’t reduce the rating to 4 stars because I really respect the option for a one-time payment for premium instead of a subscription. I hope more apps adopt that.

Best Habit tracker ever ! — This app is the best habit tracker. I’ve used ant tried most of the other ones in the App Store to find they either have a less pleasant interface than HabitKit or they have to many un-necessary features that distract from the main objective of keeping habits consistent. Having all the heat maps on the one screen in year view really allowed me to not break the chain and keep up the habits daily. The design of the app is perfect. It’s professional and easy to use. I look forwards to more creations from this developer
Simple, visual and does the job. — I only have the free version, but that is all I need.
Love this so much! — I use this app every day and it’s so satisfying to check something off! I love the ‘year in review’ part too. Definitely gonna use this forever!

Really love the app — I have been using the app for a week and love the fact UI and how easy it is to follow the UI and manage the habits. 

Love customisation of icons.. I wish there was a youtube icon as well.

Perfect for ADHD — I got inspired to use this app specifically due to the visualization of the graphs. After seeing my GitHub graph from last year, I just knew this was the right tool. It has been simply amazing for my ADHD. Great app.

Ótimo! Virou meu app de hábitos padrão — O app entrega o que propõe, com um visual muito bonito e sem complexidades desnecessárias. O plano gratuito é bom o suficiente e o preço do pro é muito justo. 
Mandei um e-mail ao desenvolvedor com uma dúvida e ele foi muito atencioso na resposta.
Excelente — Para quem gosta de um efeito visual ele é perfeito!
Great — Great app and fair prices but I wish I could see how the charts are before purchasing the pro version
Amazing! — Leaving a review to help developer. Great app, looks elegant, smooth, and quite functional. The dev answered my request for support within the day and was super friendly. Thank you!

Minimalism Perfection — I was getting sick of my inconsistent routine. Wanted to fix it. Downloaded 5-6 of the top habit tracker apps. Didn’t like any of them. Thought it was too much to ask for. Until I came across this beauty. Love the developer theme and the attention to detail with the slightly complex features making them super intuitive. Couldn’t have asked for a better experience. Got the monthly subscription then switched to yearly in a week since I’ll be keeping this.
Simple but great! — Absolutely love how simple it is, and easy to use. Very nice to look at too with the squares and columns, great job making this! Was looking for a basic habit tracker for a while
👌 — It’s very simple, colourful, clean, neat and does the job well.  I LOOOOOOOVE the fact that they don’t link any personal data & NOT a subscription model.  Thanks gang ;)

Amazing app, Great visualizations and statistics — There are many habit tracking apps that cover basic functionality, but what makes this app stand out are the visualizations and statistics/reports. The way it shows the grids with the squares along with the advanced reports for subscribers is absolutely perfect. Try it out, you won’t be disappointed.
Exactly what I needed — The app is easy to use and isn’t overly complicated. The visuals are great.

What a gem! — I’m so happy I found this app. I have adhd and the features and customization really help keep me engaged and being able to tweak things in the advanced section is perfect!! 

I absolutely love the visual grid as well. It makes my brain happy. 

Amazingly,  you also value user data and privacy and all my data stays with me?!? This is fantastic. 

5 stars - you have a new pro subscriber.

Wouldn’t it be cool? — I think it’d be cool to add options for different kind of the same habit, and being able to tell by color! Like I want to meditate everyday, but maybe today I do some alternate nostril breathing, and tmrw I do mindfulness meditation, and the next day I do natural meditation instead, and I can see which one I did by setting up the color and showing up on the widget
Gamification and visually nice — Has been working for me to keep on the habits that I want to work on
changed my life! — this app has made me become incredibly consistent with my daily and weekly habits. i can’t recommend it enough!
Great app! — A unique UI - nothing like it on the App Store. The different views  and details in the habit edit screens are fantastic. Great job developers!

Amazing for tracking — This app really been keeping me motivated. Simple to use and looking at the progress over the year, really puts everything into perspective. 
My only wish is that there was an Apple Watch app. I love getting that satisfying feeling when marking something for the day. Having it on my wrist would make it that much more easier.
Terrible unfortunately — Overpriced options for such a simplistic app with free alternatives on the App Store. Pitty there is no view that shows an entire year on screen.

Lovely App — Visually beautiful. Easy to use. I found how the streaks are calculated a little confusing but the developer got back to me quickly to explain what I was missing. By far my favourite habit tracking app.

I love it! — Love the design and how easy it is to use! I really recommend it!
Plus, the creator take time to answer question and idea, he/she andwer very fast! 
I like you can easily see more than the previous week of the tracking! That’s very encouraging!
Excellent app — Very satisfied. Thank you.

Absolutely wonderful — I am really happy with this app! I even sent an email to suggest potential future features and I got a reply right away! I will certainly be using the app every day for the next couple of years.

Love the app!! — Im loving the app alot and it gives me the visual guide I’ve been looking for. A few things I would like to be added in the future is the potential ability to add more reminders for a habit rather than just one.

P.ex: having the habit of brushing your teeth logged in and you want to do it twice a day. So instead of having one reminder you can make two reminders.

 Because we all know we are bound to forget to do it and thats 100% okay!!! ;) but other than that, amazing work and great app for folks who like visual things 🤟🏻

Simple and Effective — When I was looking for a habit tracker, this was exactly what I was envisioning. I just wanted a simple visualization of my habits in a grid, none of the random extra gimmicks in other apps- and this was it. So clean, beautiful, and simple to keep track of some good habits.

Sweet app for visual people — Love it! 
My only suggestions are already being worked on.
Funciones — Fácil de usar eso si me gustaría que le agregaran más colores en la siguiente actualización pero todo lo demás perfecto
Me encanta! — Me encanta el diseño de la app! El poder visualizar mi constancia (o falta de ella) me motiva a esforzarme y crear hábitos.

Recommend! — It’s an amazing app to keep your habits. I have tried a lot of different apps, however they didn’t really kept me going that long. I’ve been using HabitKit for half year now and it has really helped me build my habits. Especially if u have the widget it is really easy to see your habits and it’s fun in a way, as if you are to complete daily quests.

Love it, it’s exactly what I needed! — I’ve tried quite a few habit tracker apps and nothing came close to this one - It’s extremely simple to use and you can see everything important at first glance when you open the app. Also love how I can customize colors, icons and rearange the habits. 
The premium version is very reasonably priced and I was very happy to purchase it - the creator/creators of this app absolutely deserve the small support!
Perfect! — Finally beautifull graphic application exactly according to my ideas. Thank you! Good job! 🤩👍🏻

Gute App, aber ausbaufähig — Zuerst einmal, ich finde die App toll. Sie ist wirklich sehr übersichtlich und einfach gestaltet, dennoch nett anzusehen. Ich hab mir sofort die Pro Version geholt, weil ich auch noch mehr als 4 Gewohnheiten tracken wollte, da ich mein Training im Sport explizit aufteile. Da wurde ich leider dann etwas enttäuscht, ich hatte mir bei den Statistiken und Diagrammen wirklich mehr erhofft.. Super wäre, wenn man hier die einzelnen Kacheln, wie erfüllungsrate. Oder streak anklicken könnte und dann noch mehr erfährt darüber.  Ein kleiner Fließtext würde ja schon reichen. Oder dass man z.B. erfährt an welchen Wochentagen man am aktivsten ist/ eine Gegenüberstellung von verschiedenen Gewohnheiten. Einfach mehr Aufschlüsselumg und Analysen. Das erhoffe ich mir bei 35€ einmalkauf zukünftig schon. Alles in allem, aber trotzdem eine tolle App und so wie ich es in den anderen Rezensionen lese wird sich ja auch weiterhin darum gekümmert die App zu verbessern. 
Danke :)

Top - Checkbox — Eine wirklich angenehme App ohne viel schnick Schnack, der einzige schnick Schnack der aber toll wäre, ist eine Art Checkbox bspw.
Titel:
Morgenroutine
(Innerhalb dieses Habits unter Habits erstellen)
- 1 Glas Wasser 
- Gesicht waschen 
- Zähneputzen 
- Mobilty 

So hat man in diesem bsp. 4 Habits innerhalb einer „großen“ Kategorie

Bisher das BESTE — Ich bin ehrlich? Die App stillt meine autistischen Züge maximal. Alles was ich brauche ist da. Extrem benutzerfreundlich. So benutzerfreundlich, dass ich mehrere Minuten den Bildschirm angestarrt habe und mir gedacht habe „das ist wirklich die benutzerfreundlichste App die ich kenne, wieso ist die so benutzerfreundlich?“

Jetzt mal ehrlich, man sieht einen Jahresüberblick und einen Wochenüberblick und das auf Anhieb. Man erkennt sofort wie man gerade steht mit seiner Disziplin. Es ist wirklich brutal übersichtlich. 

Lediglich mehr Farben wäre ein nettes extra und: das ist jetzt extrem spezifisch aber: wenn man hier noch die Funktion integrieren könnte, dass man bei Erinnerungen die Gebetszeiten für den aktuellen Ort bestimmen kann und nicht nur feste Zeiten - so dass sich die App von der zentralen Datenserver die Zeiten zieht (jede Gebetszeiten App hat das, ist bestimmt nichts kompliziertes) dann wäre das ein unfassbarer gamechanger.  Potenziell 2 Milliarden Kunden hätte man mehr dadurch.

Lieb das Design und die App 💜 — Minimalistisches Design, Personalisierung und alles da was man braucht, um täglich erreichte Ziele zu tracken. Vor allem im Dark Mode knallen die Farben so schön raus. Es macht Spaß zu sehen, wie das Pattern täglich wächst 💪

Simplest ADHD and habit tool on the market — I’ve been using it for two years now and track anything from good habits (running, climbing, supplements), bad habits and daily chores. Saves my forgettable adhd brain. And Sebastian (the man behind HabitKit) is super quick to respond and takes feedback serious.

The iOS widgets are amazing for the main habits you’d want to keep track of. Ps: there’s always new useful updates coming

Sehr gute App - leider bis jetzt nur für „good“ Habits ausgelegt — Schön gemachte App, funktioniert super und es gibt die Möglichkeit Tasks/Habits auch nur teilweise zu erledigen, was in der Übersicht sehr schön durch eine blassere Farbe dargestellt wird

Perfekt wäre die App wenn es auch die Option gäbe, Gewohnheiten die man sich abgewöhnen möchte als „Bad Habits“ zu kategorisieren (ist natürlich auch so möglich aber macht einem entweder die Statistiken kaputt oder man negiert die Gewohnheit und muss sie dann aber jeden Tag anklicken was psychologisch wahrscheinlich suboptimal ist) und es dann darauf bezogen Streaks gäbe, wie lange man schon „clean“ ist

Nicht nötig aber schön wäre es außerdem ein großes Widget zu haben, welches alle Gewohnheiten gleichzeitig als sehr kleine Pixel zb für ein ganzes Jahr anzeigt

(Ich habe das bezahlte Upgrade aktiviert und kann es empfehlen)
Cool — Finally an app where I actually tracked my progress for over 6 months. Thanks Seb

Perfekter Tracker — Optisch sehr schön und doch minimalistisch gehaltener Tracker. Gerade der Contribution Graph / Heatmap freut das Entwicklerherz und motiviert.

Kleiner Feature Request.
Wäre es möglich mehr als eine Erinnerung für ein Habit hinzuzufügen? Bsp. Habit A mit Erinnerung Mo-Fr: 19:00 sowie Sa-So: 08:00
Momentan muss man dafür anscheinend das Habit duplizieren.

Perfekter Habit Tracker — Der Habit Tracker hat wirklich alles was man braucht. Selten schreibe ich Rezensionen. Und noch seltener hole ich mir eine Pro Version einer App, die auch kostenlos gut funktioniert. 
Ich hatte früher immer in meinem Bullet Journal meine Habits getrackt, ebenfalls in einem Pixel Format und dann am Ende des Jahres eine Jahresübersicht gezeichnet. Die App übernimmt das alles für mich. Und mit den Widgets bin ich jeden Tag motiviert am Abend alle meine Sachen abzuhaken. Als jemand mit ADHS hatte ich schon immer Schwierigkeiten mit Routinen. Und sämtliche Apps mit Notifications bringen bei mir nichts. Umso schöner zu sehen, dass so eine simple App mir Freude macht, meine Gewohnheiten zu Tracken und meine Routinen weiter auszubauen. Hier wurde wirklich an alles gedacht und trotzdem so schön simpel und Userfreundlich. Das unterstütze ich gerne mit einem Abo :)

Best Habit Tracker Out There — In my opinion, this is the nicest designed habit tracker app currently available. Its user interface is very intuitive and appealing. The pro version offers detailed summary plots for each habit and yearly reviews.
Best Habit App on the Market — I have tried a lot of apps over the years but this is the only one that helped me consistently establishing habits in my life. The widgets are perfect.

My All-Time Favourite — Clear structure. All necessary functions. And unbeatable design.
No other app can keep up with that!
I love the unique approach of displaying the calendar as dots.

I like it, but no icloud sync, no native ipad adaptation — I like the style of the app and the really excellent handling of the entries. These were the deciding factors for me to spend the 35 euros on the Pro version. Unfortunately, I only realised afterwards that there is no iCloud sync with the iPad and that the iPad App does not adapt to the bigger display. The iPhone view on the iPad is not very nice. 
If the Pro version cost €5 or even €10, I would still be happy with it. But for 35 euros I would like to have the synchronisation and the adaptation to the iPad.

Very cool App — I've tried out a lot of different Habit Tracker Apps and for me this ones the best so far. I used it for a year now and like how minimalistic it is and especially that you can have an overview of all your habits for the last year oder so in one overview and i like that you can turn of the streaks for individual habits. That way I can track bad habits without being rewarded for doing them times in a row 😅. The only feature I would like to have is a note feature so that you can take notes on how you achieved something or while mood tracking, why you had a good/bad day.

Beste App für die Etablierung von Habits — Ich hab schon einige Apps für das Habit-Tracking ausprobiert, aber HabitKit gefällt mir bei weitem am Besten. Das UI, der Minimalismus der App und die farbenfrohe Darstellung gefällt mir mega gut.

Außerdem ist der Entwickler einer super netter Dude, der einem bei Problemen schnell hilft. Ich hatte einen Bug in den Widgets gemeldet und zwei Tage später gab es einen Fix. Klasse!

I really love the app — Love the functionality, ease of use and optics (especially for progress overview). Feels great to set a habit done. I tried around 10 other apps. Some are better in some way or another. But as overall package the HabitKit works great for me.
Great design and user experience — I love the github-like grid view of your habit completions. The whole app is designed really well!

Sehr gute App — Ich finde die App sehr toll und nutze sie jeden Tag. Eine coole Idee wäre noch, dass man jeden Tag angeben kann, wie oft man was gemacht hat und dass die Farbe dann etwas dunkler erscheint je öfter es gemacht wurde. Also wenn ich z.B. angebe ich mache eine bestimmte Task 1 mal am Tag, habe sie aber 3 mal gemacht, dass man das dann auch sehen kann.

Best visual app so far — I tried several apps and this one is the most appealing for me.

One thing I’m missing ist the possibility to silence a reminder when I’ve done my task already. For example if my plan is to do something once per week I would expect my reminder to be silent for the rest of the week once I’ve marked it as completed.

It would also be nice if the visual tracker would scale with the number of occurrences. I’d like to have just one block per week if my occurrence ist just once per week, etc…

Simple and effective! — Have been using the app for the last few months and absolutely in love with it. Also, the feedback support from Sebastian is unparalleled! He takes out the time to respond to the feedback, which to me is unheard of.

Simple, good looking , great for good overview — Does exactly what it claims and is well designed so you can get a quick overview of all your tasks and their frequency in one picture. Feature request - please record the time of each task when completed!

Super! Sehr clean, mit ein paar Verbesserungsmöglichkeiten — Ich habe mir die App gerade runtergeladen und liebe es, wie klar & simpel das Design ist! Was den Tracker jetzt noch perfekt für mich machen würde:

- Synchronisierung über iCloud

- Abhaken der Habits direkt im Widget. Der Haken wird ja schon angezeigt, nur springt man dann erstmal in die App, wenn man drauftippt.

- Auswahl, welchen Zeitraum das Raster darstellt. Ich würde es z. B. am liebsten immer monatsweise sehen. Vielleicht auch mit einer Option, nach von & hinten zu blättern. Merkwürdig finde ich auch, dass der erste Tag nach Anlegen eines neuen Habit irgendwo mitten im Raster angezeigt wird.

Simply the best! — I tried so so many habit trackers but they are either complicated with too many functions and just too all over the place. They also don’t really motivate you enough to keep going. This app shows your progress right under the habit. The progress for many months!!! not just for the current week. This way, you don’t feel discouraged if you have been off track for one entire week or maybe longer. This amazing design of the app promotes a healthy mindset which I just love. I bought the lifetime subscription. It is just worth it and I am happy to support the app developer. Much respect!

Best Habit Tracker on the Market — I never managed to stick to habits for a long time. But with HabitKit and the unique visualization, it works much better. If you're a developer, the whole thing feels very familiar from GitHub, which makes it easy to find your way around without much explanation.

Super Habit Tracker! — Nutze HabitKit jetzt seit mehreren Wochen und bin immer noch fasziniert vom Grid Layout (was für eine geile Idee) und dem allgemeinen Design. Es macht einfach Spaß und motiviert. Vielen Dank für diese App!
Ich hoffe, dass sie schnell in den Rankings aufsteigt. Liebe Grüße, Jay

Intuitiv und simpel - so muss es sein! — Wenn ich Vorsätze und Ziele habe, die ich verfolgen will, sollte für die Methodik/Verwaltung nicht mehr Zeit drauf gehen als unbedingt nötig. Das gelingt mit dieser App: Habit benennen, Farbe und Icon wählen und schon kann es losgehen! Übersichtlich und auf das Wesentliche reduziert. Für mich genau das richtige. 

Für das Angebot einer Einmalzahlung als Alternative zum Abomodell würde ich nochmal einen Bonus-Stern vergeben, wenn ich könnte.

Me está ayudando muchismo — La verdad es que no tenía muy claro si la aplicación me iba a venir bien o no, y ha sido todo un acierto, el pagarla y al usarla.

El que se tan fácil de usar y tan visual para poder ver los hábitos que has hecho o no, me está ayudando muchísimo a seguir con ellos.

Aún le faltan incorporar funcionalidades, pero el autor me ha confirmado que están en ello.

Recomendada 100%

Motiva a mantenerte constante — Esta app es súper simple pero muy efectiva a la hora de motivarte a mantener la constancia en aquellas actividades que quieres introducir en tu rutina. Ver cómo se va llenando la cuadrícula resulta tan satisfactorio que te pensarás dos veces si fallar un solo día 🔥
Perfecta! — Es una app muy visual y fácil de usar. Funciona de maravilla. De las mejores que he visto!

Simple, functional and visually pleasing — I have never before encountered such a functional yet aesthetically pleasing and simple tracker app. I love the colours and the ability to group trackers.
This is exactly what I have been looking for, thank you.

Meilleur habit tracker — Sous un format GitHub, il est facile de tracer ses habitudes et de voir son évolution sur le temps. Je n’écris pas énormément de review mais de toutes les applications que j’ai, c’est très certainement ma préférée et la meilleure.

An easy to use habit tracker — The app is not intrusive, not forcing ads or notifications on you every hour (unless you create your own reminders to complete a habit!)
It’s a joy to use for its simplicity, while still being highly configurable (number of completion per day/week/month/…, length of a streak, past completion display…)

Awesome: Simple, Powerful, and Worth Every Cent — I’ve tested more than ten habit-tracking apps over the years. Most of them are too complex, with far too many options and interactions, which in the end makes you lose the motivation to keep using them (you end up spending more time on the app than actually doing your habits — pointless). Here, you get the essentials, with plenty of features that are very well thought out and seamlessly integrated.

There’s just one element missing that I find essential. You can set a habit to be done X times per day, week, or month. But when it’s set weekly or monthly, there’s no clear indication that you’ve actually achieved the goal. It should be subtly visible when looking at the dashboard.

Of course, I’m giving it 5/5, because even without this feature, the app is fantastic, and I truly hope the developer will continue improving it for a long time.

I’m eagerly waiting for the MacOS version (and maybe one day WatchOS).

Get the Pro version to support and reward the developer’s work. The price is more than fair for the value it can bring to your life!

Top1 Habit Tracking App — I love how the app is designed. The habit tracking is great. I find the interface addictive. Tracking habits with this kind of interface, with the little colored squares each day, is really enjoyable. You can see your progress clearly.
La meilleure pour moi, pas forcément pour vous — J’ai utilisé beaucoup d’applications de ce genre mais celle là c’est celle que je voulais avoir ! Merci aux développeurs.

Super app — Bonne appli! J’aime bien le format un peu comme sur GitHub qui permet d’avoir une vue directe sur ses données.

Ça serait cool de pouvoir faire des inputs également de nombres. Par exemple, aujourd’hui j’ai bu (nombre) cafés. Je peux tracker non seulement l’habitude mais aussi le nombre si jamais je veux tracker un nombre quotidien. 
Quid de l’option du input de numéro en plus du cochage.

Je recommande l’appli!

Decent enough — I like the app and the design works for me, mostly. I’m planning of using Premium for a month to see how I like it, so these are my initial thoughts…
I currently have 5 habits and I need to scroll to see the 5th, so this is a bit annoying. I’m not sure how many days are displayed (just counted - around 200) but I would like the option to reduce this so more habits can fit without having to scroll.
Some stats / graphs would also be nice.
I can imagine the main screen would be quite motivating once you start building up the habits.
Thanks
chex  boxe — Un jour passer je doit plus pouvoir cocher la tache que j’ai excité ou pas sa m’obligerai à cocher les taches le joule jour . Sinon j’aime vôtre application
Almost everything that you could hope for in a Habit Tracker — All I would say is missing is a weekly tracking option. So instead of by day, you can track a certain habit that is weekly.
Good but needs work — Good but needs to be able to see clear overview faster

You WILL Achieve your goals — I love this app for the sole reason you can track your habits, and see them progress over time as it provides a basis which motivates you to get up and achieve your goals every day.

Eventually, i paid for premium (which is by no means necessary), to both support the creator and also display the widgets; helping so much more as every day i could see my progress, reminding me to do the actions leading me towards my goals.

I have been able to focus on my goals (for example this is the first time i have ever gone to the gym every day for a week), and has helped me throughout the journey of achieving my goals.

By far the best habit tracker on this app, as you can go your own pace and set it up yourself fully. Could not recommend more!
Great habit tracker — Nice visually appealing grid layouts make habit tracking easy and effective!

Amazing for my ADHD Brain! — I don’t usually write reviews but I just wanted to share how well this app works for someone like me who picks tasks/hobbies up and then drops them the next week.

The same could be said for apps, I’ve had a lot of habit and tracker apps that I go all in on and then once again I drop them. But this one has truly been awesome and I can’t wait to log my colourful square each day.

Maybe that’s it, maybe it’s because it’s just so simple and it LOOKS good too - I think the simplicity works and it looks awesome in dark mode. I’m tracking my calorie defecit, medication and exercise.

best I've tried, but no sync across devices — Intuitive and good customization.  All of my goals are x number of times per week -- not daily nor tied to a specific day of the week.  The numeric streak count for weekly goals is strange, so I don't use it.  But at least the graphical boxes can show me if I'm where I want to be or not.  But I really wish that the app would sync across devices!!  That is the one feature that I'm sorely missing.
Great app — The ui is very clean and it’s satisfying to watch the calendars fill up!
Excellent — great way to visually see progress and keep track of streaks, very easy and satisfying to use

Best tracker out there — Hands down one of the best habit trackers that I’ve found out there. The user interface is very intuitive and easy to use. It has absolutely everything I was looking for.
1. Ability to set daily, weekly or monthly goals.
2. Ability to create a goal that requires multiple completions to count toward a streak (i.e. taking meds—you can create two instances that go toward one goal).
3. Reminders that you can create to help you remember to complete your goal. Let’s face it some of us get busy and lose track of things we want to do during the day and this helps immensely.

These functions are in the pro version which is completely worth it, without a doubt.
Exactly what I was looking for — This app is really well done, intuitive, feature rich, and has a beautiful interface. Really appreciate the widget support, and analytics views to help recap

Almost perfect - Few updates needed — I first downloaded HabitKit in the ending of March 2025. I bought the lifetime premium version. When I first downloaded the app, it didn't have an option for putting your own emojis for habits, which was really frustrating. I'm very happy that they finally put an emoji update. I was tired of using a dog bone for my seafood habit. My issue with the new update is that you can't change the skin color of the emojis. It's also disappointing that you can't choose a set of Crayola like colors for your habits including brown, instead of the preset pastel colors that is given. No true red or solid purples just a pastel palette for everything... I also think that the counter for 1, 5, 10 , 15 shouldn't be there. I think that instead the only option should be to set your own number of "Pages read" for each habit. It would look much better for the eyes that way. Or at least give the option to turn it off and only have your own preset number. I also think that the HabitKit wrapped should be worded better and upgraded. Besides those things, this is a decent app for habit tracking. I do also believe having a bad habit tracker section or page would be great, and helpful for separation of good and bad habits. Plus not being able to sync to iCloud is hella wack. I can only give 2 stars because I know it could be better.

The Perfect App For What I Needed — This app on my phone has been insanely helpful and so easy to use. I can track anything going on in my life and then easily look back over the history of my habit. Things like how frequently I’m vacuuming or if I took my medication each day or week. Every time I login and track my habits it also reminds me of things I might not have done yet like…oh I haven’t done that thing yet today. So I often get up to start or finish something because I see that it isn’t checked off for the day. 

What makes this app better than others I was looking at is that I’m 100% choosing my own categories and specific tasks. So my weird and wonderful lists are tailored perfectly to me, and there isn’t anything extraneous. 

The only complaint I have is that the data is only on your device. So I can see and use it on my phone but I can’t pull it up on my tablet or computer. I reached out to the developers and they say they hope to change this in the future. So fingers crossed, this app could get even better.

Best habit app you will find! — I’ve genuinely tried all the habit apps- simple ones, complex ones, gamified ones, expensive ones — and HabitKit is easily the best of the bunch.

The grid based visual tracking is brilliant. It’s simple, motivating, and incredibly satisfying to look at. No unnecessary fluff, no overwhelming features- just a beautifully designed system that actually makes you want to stay consistent.

Customization is excellent, the UI is clean and intuitive, and it strikes the perfect balance between powerful and easy to use. This is the first habit app I’ve stuck with long term.

If you’re serious about building habits (or breaking bad ones), stop searching. HabitKit is it.

Does one thing and does it well! — Interface is clean and responsive, the app doesn’t feel sluggish at all. Records your data smoothly and then shows it to you how you want it, exactly how a habit tracker should. Developer is active and responsive to feedback. Pro subscription offers a lifetime option which is greatly appreciated in a sea of apps and services where you keep paying up every month for no additional value and could lose features if you don’t go up a tier at any time.

Simple, reliable and beautifully designed — Been using HabitKit daily for 2 years now and it’s become my go-to habit tracker. Clean interface, no bloat, just works. The widget support is excellent for quick check-ins.

One small wish: a basic read-only API would open up automation possibilities for power users, but that’s a nice-to-have.

Highly recommended for anyone serious about building habits.

Good — It’s a good app! I have the pro version and as much as I enjoy it, I do not feel that the pro version should cost as much as it does. The app does not have enough features to justify the $13 pro. $5 or $10 would be more acceptable. Also, there is a fixed amount of colors that you can make your habits that you’re tracking, and of the 21 available colors, 4 of them are just different shades of grey. I really wish there was access to a color wheel or something so you can select more colors. The blues and greens that are available are way too similar. I, and I’m sure many others, need a lot of visual variety when tracking habits like this. And when you’re tracking over 10 habits, it gets difficult to visually distinguish between 4 shades of grey and 6 shades of mildly different blueish green

Great habit tracker!  Worth the price — I spontaneously bought the lifetime access because I want to start tracking certain daily and weekly things I wanted to do or not do.  I have been using for 2 months now every day.  It’s great! 

It’s customizable, yet not confusing.  As a UX/UI designer myself, I appreciate the balance of simplicity and flexibility. 

Only improvements I’d love to see are the ability to have an anti-streak calculator for habits I’m trying to break, and some more robust reporting in terms of trends.

Overall a great, daily app!  Get it!

Best hair tracker app — Awesome app, better than Atoms and all the other habit trackers. The price to unlock all features ($2/month, $12/year) is reasonable and affordable. I upgraded to the yearly subscription after trying it out for a week. This is fun to use which means I’ll keep using it. I like that you can add a corresponding emoji to each habit and include a habit description. I also like that you can set streak goals in multiple ways. This app just has all the best features. I’m thankful it exists.

No bad habit tracking and No Apple Watch support. — I’m dissatisfied with the app. I purchased only to find out that it does not include bad habit tracking, only requires you to use work around. The app also does not have an Apple Watch app. Please integrate these and I will update my review.

Great but lacks cloud syncing — Really great app but lacks cloud syncing which seems crazy for an app entering 2026 and is the main reason I am hesitant to pay for the premium subscription. I also don’t understand how the app counts streaks for “x times per week” habits. I’m on a 12 week streak for a habit I started 8 weeks ago.

Simple is Beautiful — This app checks a few boxes for me:
It allows me to see the trends of my habits over time; allowing me to see what i need to improve or fix. 
I can easily keep track of habits in multiple areas of my life, from working out, studying, and down to simple things like remembering to water my plants. 

While I can use notes, or a to-do list, or alarms, HabitKit allows you to come to one place for all of that-in a more fun and satisfying place. 

Honestly, the colors, icons, calendar, and organization through putting habits in certain categories keeps everything neat and aesthetically pleasingly. Everyone has their way of doing what this app does, but the way habit kit does it is what allows me to use it this thoroughly. Actually, it makes keeping in touch with my goals and to-dos fun-something lacking from other apps whether pre-installed, or otherwise. 

Being able to see your goals and habits stack up or lack over time is the big indicator on how well/poor Im doing, and thats the motivator for however you choose to track your trends. 

Long time user of the app, and I’ll keep on using it to perfect my routine. Well done Habitkit, looking forward to future updates that reflect the simple brilliance you have here already.

Could be SO MUCH BETTER — I know the app isn't abandoned, but it feels abandoned. No cloud sync or cloudkit. No Mac app. No bad habit mode that automatically checks off days. No custom icon support (icon library very limited). No custom colors. It just feels abandoned. With a couple weekends of work the developer could be making double what they are making now with a few tweaks. C'mon!

A Game Changer — I recently turned started using a minimalist phone setup to help me to be more productive. A key part of the design was adding HabitKit widgets to my home screen. It's very motivating to see your habit history packed into a beautiful little chart, with the ability to check off (or increment) habits without having to open the app. After making these changes to my phone, this past week has been the most productive week of my life, and I sincerely believe HabitKit has been the main reason for that. 

The support is also incredible. I reached out to the solo developer via email, asking him about 2 different features I was hoping he could add to the app. 2 days later, he got back to me, in a very friendly and well-thought-out email. In this email, he told me that he had already been working on adding the first feature, and the other had been added to his todo list. Given that he is a solo developer, and also working on another up-and-coming app at the same time, I'd say his support services are the best I've ever seen, from any app on the app store.

Great app, some suggestions — Seriously loving this app so far - it’s pretty much exactly what I was looking for. Thank you for offering a one-time purchase option - it’s rare these days and you’re awesome for that

Two suggestions:

> negative habits
- basically the opposite of a regular habit, allowing you to set a limit for how many times a day, if any before the color turns off
- this could even be as simple as a habit that auto-completes at the start of the day, but you can go back and manually uncheck it

> web app
- it’s a big ask, but even just like a dashboard accessible on the web would be fantastic

keep up the good work

Best habit tracker out there — HabitKit is by far the best habit tracker I have used… and I have used several. It is sleek and simple, yet customizable. 

The options for viewing my habits are perfect for the ways in which I think about them- in both the short and long term. I can manage my day-to-day easily with a high-level, consolidated view of all my habits, while still being able to see the big picture over an extended period of time with a GitHub-esque chart. 

Bonus points for a responsive developer, and continued improvements. Highly recommend.

Very good — I’ve been looking for a good Habit tracking app on iOS. I tested seven and ended up choosing this one. I really like the simplicity, aesthetic, straightforwardness, and overall good usability of this app. Also the pro version is also of the cheapest out there. $2 a month, or $30 lifetime. Compared to $10 a month and $90 lifetime pro versions. I recommend it!

HabitKit + Automations = SUCCESS — HabitKit is hands-down the best habit app I’ve used. It has enabled me to set up old hotel key cards as NFC triggers — when I tap one for my morning supplements, it marks the habit complete, reads the weather, starts my playlist, and tells me my calendar for the day. Everything just flows. The design is clean, automations work flawlessly, and the developer is super responsive. Absolutely worth it!

Reliable and Pretty — I’ve been using it for a month and haven’t seen any bugs. I love the visual style more than any other habit app, and it’s the main reason I chose it. HabitKit just feels good to use, and that’s important for an app you use daily.
Nice App but Lacking — I really like this app, it reminds me of GitHub but I wish the widgets allowed me to see more then one habit at a time, or gave me a overview.

Easy, motivating, and ad free — I’ve been using this app for almost two months now to track the days I drink enough water. The layout itself is pretty self explanatory and simple, and the lack of ads makes it very easy to log on and check off a streak without distractions and wasting time. The free version of Habitkit works very well if you have a few habits you want to track, and works perfect despite not being premium. I personally hate when developers force users into buying a subscription for the basic features their app has been made to offer by nagging with constant ads and an overall worse experience with the app, so Habitkit is one of the rare gems among many slop apps who suffer from such issues.

Thank you, developer!
Una aplicación Magnífica — La app se ajusta a lo que uno busca perfectamente, visualmente es muy bonito y moderno, llevo meses usándolo y estoy muy contento, felicitaciones a los creadores

Form and Function 🤌🏼 — HabitKit has been able to accomplish something that no other habit tracker has: I actually use it. The layout is so useful and logical, with all of the distracting junk stripped away. Its simplicity does not make it any less powerful, however. In fact, I think that is the thing that propels HabitKit ahead of all the others in terms of excellence. It strikes the perfect balance of simple and functional/customizable while also being beautiful. 

Data is powerful, but only if you can actually collect it. Now, I can.
Good app-with paid version — I love seeing the grids as a way to visualize consistency! I have the paid version of the app, can't speak to the limits of the free version. Solid app.

One of the best habit tracking apps - but NEEDS iOS Reminders integration and maybe APIs exposed ? — This is by far the most visually appealing app. I was actually going to develop my own app which was similar to this, where it had the altair heatmap chart. But this goes beyond my initial idea and also has step counts/tiered counting. Moreover, the ease of completing a task with a tap, setting of reminders, color coding and the availability to switch between three different views is exactly what I needed.

This is way better than todoist, it is simple and intuitive. Most other apps have a lot of clutter and have too many details and clunky interfaces.

One important feature that is missing though is its integration with Calendar and Reminders. Not just that, PLEASE expose APIs to interact with the data, this would have a limited use case, but still could be very useful. For example, one could ingest their daily step count and automatically mark a habit. Another example is that say if I want to block a particular app unless I do X, it could allow it to do so. Lets say that I have a habit like “no scrolling videos in the morning for 2 hours”, I should be able to enforce this and mark the habit only when certain conditions outside the app are met - I know this is a little outside the scope of this app and probably would fit into another “habit enforcer” app that could integrate with this, but in any case this requires REST APIs to be exposed. I would love to partner with the dev and work on this idea.

Just right — This app is the exact thing I needed. It is simple and provides a visualization of goals. I can even quickly show the extent to which I reached a goal per day. Try it! It might be just what you’re looking for.

Great design and updates — HabitKit is an awesome app if you like tracking your progress on anything. The UI is excellent and continues to receive quality updates, and the widgets are super convenient. The summary analytics are also a really nice touch. Easily worth the purchase price.

Very confusing — Way too much going on for something as simple as tracking “habits” the app is eye appealing, but anyone who wants to use it should not go through so much trouble trying to understand it. I still haven’t figured it out and I will be deleting after this review.

Simple, Perfect — This app is exactly what I was looking for: a way to visually understand my habits over time where I'm doing well, where I need to pick it up. It's extremely simple and simple to use. Not only that but the developer is extremely responsive. I sent him an email about something that I wanted, and he responded the next day. 5/5. Download this app if you're looking for any type of habit tracker.
Great graphics! — Clearly shows my progress toward my nutrition goal.

Convert — I was skeptical at first on whether this app would be what I was looking for in a habit app. Some try to do too much and some are too watered down. This hits the right chord with me. Great UI. Especially a home view with a month’s worth of performance in one easy glance.

Love it, but have suggestions! — I love the set up, if you like the green squares of GitHub, this habit tracker is for you. However, I think it would be amazing if they implemented a folder or categorization feature. I want my career growth habits to be separate from my health and wellness habits.

Best way to visualize progress — This app is great for visualizing and tracking your habits in a multitude of different ways. I really like and value the customization aspect as well, and being able to see my growth never fails to boost my mood!
Easy to use — This app is very simple and easy to use, but so versatile!

Great app, needs syncing. — Really great, functional app with beautiful widgets. Does its job in an easy to use, visually pleasing way on my phone. 

Once it gets an iPad app and iCloud syncing, which the dev says is on the roadmap, it’ll be a 5-star app!

The only habit tracker that makes me feel good! — I have tried many habit trackers but this is the only one that doesn't give me so much anxiety and stress when I miss my streaks. A lot of the other ones try to hold you accountable and stick to goals. While I do wanna do that, some days just make it hard and my busy schedule makes it hard to keep up with everything. HabitKit on the other hand lets you actually just keep tabs on your progress. Yes, maybe you missed a day or week, but you can always see your previous progress and remind yourself that you can still make it up and catch up! It's no surprise that other apps are copying this now! Sebastian's also a really responsive and friendly founder! Really happy to get to support this project!

Perfect for smart goals — I use this app to review weekly smart goals. It’s perfect and does the job of tracking and presenting attractive reports quite well.  It’s not ideal for project management or to do lists, but does habits better than any other of the 20 apps I auditioned. I got the paid version and feel it’s worth it.

Needs more color options — Nearly perfect…Would gladly pay for pro or lifetime if it meant I could choose custom colors for habits. As I use widgets to help me stay on track, I need an app that will fit with the color scheme of my background. Unfortunately this is not that app.
Amazing app — I’ve tested a lot of tracker and this one offers the best UX and visualization while keeping it simple and intuitive to use.

Simple, Effective, and Visually Elegant — UPDATE (2025-02-05)

Not sure how long I’ve been using HabitKit (just checked and it has been a bit over two years) and I’m still loving it ♥️

It’s simple, has the features I want, and zero bloat. I love that you can enable/disable streaks because I’m no longer doing streaked habits.

I’ve been using it as a widget stack on my Home Screen (small size, all habits in the stack) and it’s just perfect like this!

—=•=— 

I’ve been using the “don’t break the chain” method of habit building for about a billion years. I’ve used apps and my own paper trackers. They all work, more or less, but some just feel better than others, and with something simple like habit tracking, feel is 90% of what’s important.

HabitKit has FEEL son!

There’s something about the simplicity of the app and the ease of logging that just feels right. But more than that, the visual display of your streak is the best I’ve come across. It’s RIGHT in your face. There’s no ignoring it… and that’s a very very good thing.

Best habit tracker i found — Overall this is the best habit tracker i found and i went thought a lot. It helps so much to visualize your habit consistency which not many other apps have. This app also does not come with the extra un needed fluff but one thing i would like to see is an option to mark that I did not complete one of my tasks that day such as a red dot. Overall great app!

Instant behavior mod — Literally making me drink more water and workout more and do more healthy things because of how rewarding the colors and boxes are! I’m obsessed! I only just downloaded it, and I never write reviews for things, but this just deserved it. Also LOVE GitHub and coding and I can totally relate to the people who developed this app! Probably gonna purchase for life.

Great habit app after getting past initial confusion. — Setting up a habit is confusing & unintuitive. This app looks very cool, but should be easier and more clear for new users to set up. Some sort of onboarding or tutorial would be helpful, perhaps even a throwaway habit should be pre-populated so it’s easier to see how to set one up.

Update: After the initial confusion, I’ve concluded that I really like this app. I’ve even paid for a year subscription. I’ve increased my rating from 3 to 4 stars.

Perfect middle between great design and intuitive simplicity — I tried several habit trackers before committing to HabitKit. It doesn’t gamify every little feature. It’s largely unopinionated in how you use it. The design is sleek and elegant and has just enough color to motivate your lizard brain to “fill more squares”. It’s gotten me more on track than any other app.

Best Habit Tracker I've Used — The simplicity and flexibility of this app is unmatched. After trying many other habit trackers, this is the first that I've been able to use consistently without wishing it worked differently!

A recent reviewer mentioned that the app had Apple Shortcuts integrations, which is a total game changer. I hope to create Strava, Oura, and Duolingo workflows in Shortcuts to automatically mark my habits as completed.

Thanks so much for this great app, Sebastian! 🙌

Excellent simple interface — The interface is well made and the premium version is very reasonably priced. This app is not a complex task tracker and that is a good thing, it is light weight and does one thing well.

This app isn’t “the key” — I went into this thinking that this would be the app of all apps, that it would solve all my habits issues, it doesn’t. I spent something like $30 to get it on my homepage for a year(stupid, right?), and it does what it’s supposed to, but not much more
Great App for Habit Tracking — I love the visuals on the app to help track habits. The widget is great as well. The developer is responsive and the features in the pipeline are prioritized

Great App for Stacking New Habits — Over the years I have tried numerous streak apps from the productivity category.  Most have a poor interface and/or leave much to be desired.  Habitkit breathes new life into what is normally a boring, mundane task.  The simple minimalist design is right on for my needs.  I used the app for about 6 weeks before purchasing the upgrade seems well worth the extra cost.  Unlocking a bit more features but not over-complicating it too much....I'm pleased with it and looking forward to staying on track.

Pretty simple and solid — I just recently started using this app because I like the UX and how it easily conveys how often you are doing something similar to GitHub. So far I really enjoy it and I am excited to keep tracking my habits 🤞🏽
One thing I wish there was is the ability to have a widget that can display multiple habits even if in a condensed list view or something similar. I would also like to see if there is any way to add the ability on making a habit to quit something (I.e create a habit and I want to make sure that I don’t do this habit more than x amount of times per week/month/day etc. or something similar. Basically if I stay under my set limit then the habit is considered complete or good)
Awesome Visualizations — Great app, love the visualization options! It’s so satisfying to see your streaks filling up that grid.

Best habit tracker out there — I’ve been through many habit trackers over the years and they never seem to stick or work for me. This is the first one that has been simple and intuitive to use and follow. This one just clicks for me. Definitely try it out.

Incredibly Satisfying — I’ve tried many habit apps, and I think HabitKite simplistic approach is what keeps me using it. 

Many of the others (even Atoms from James Clear) is over complicated and almost… distracting. 

But with HabitKit I really just want to fill in the boxes. 

The UX is smooth, it’s easy to customize and really does “simple habit tracking” really well. 

I’ve also followed Sebastian’s journey for quite some time, and his ability to continue improving such a simple app and respond to users is something most indie apps lack. 

Can’t recommend this app enough.

This is what will get me completing New Years Resolutions — I always struggled finding a good habit tracker app, because all the dedicated ones look bad, or their feature set was never that large. They’d just be glorified counter apps. 

So once I tried this one I was so filled with glee to see a beautiful dark mode, a git esque visualization with different views, great sorting, etc. 

Instantly went for the pro subscription cause I wanted to add habits for everything, highly recommend this one

HabitKit Review — Simple effective app with a pleasant design. I don’t use all the features, just track a few daily habits. I asked the developer a question via email and he was very kind in his reply.

Really good, could be amazing - just a few small fixes — Let’s be clear, if you want to gamify a habit in a very pretty way (Ala GitHub contributions), this is the best. But there are a few feature requests/suggestions that could make it better.

#1 - Basic iPad support. Does need to be a lot, but something that better fits landscape for iPad would be appreciated. 

#2 - Synchronization - You can run the app on iOS/macOS/iPad. But there is no way to sync. Especially as a pro feature, it’d be nice to have a built in sync. 

#3 - Watch app. Again - Something super simple as a way to tick off the tasks done would be really nice when doing those exercise type habits.

It’s great — I paid for pro almost immediately after starting to use it. The dot grid is such a great way to get a feel for how good you’ve been about keeping up with your habit goals and then there’s all these detailed stats you get on top of that. The design of the app is great too, very easy to use and and simple enough that you aren’t distracted from the info you’re looking at. It’s worth the cost of the pro version for sure. It would be cool to get some new themes to play with and be able to set multiple reminders for habits that have multiple completions in a day but I’m sure the developer already has that in mind for future updates.
It Helps to Improve Your good habits — It is like GitHub of Habit
$2 a month — Too pricy for me, twice the cost of same subscription on android.

Nice but limited app — I like this app, overall nice concept and interface but not all of my goals are a binary yes/no outcome. Would be nice to track goals that are performance based, where I could enter an number and the chart will reflect performance relative to the goal figure, above target would be more saturated below target lower color saturation (ie audit 10 customers per day, input is actual # audited could be > or < goal)

10/10 Customer Satisfaction — If you’re looking to change your life, “atomic habits” style, then you need this app. Not the other habit trackers.. you need this one. This one right here is the best. 

I honestly can’t remember what the free version is like because I saw the value of upgrading within a week of downloading.

I’ve added HabitKit widgets all across my phone and not only have I see my productivity increase, but my lifestyle and mindset have greatly benefited from using this app. 

If Apple were to release a habit tracking app, it wouldn’t compare to this one. It’s sleek, easily customizable, and it’s just an overall better application compared to other habit trackers on the App Store.

If you’re NOT a fan of subscription based services, then THIS IS THE APP FOR YOU. I made a one time payment and this developer has continued to push out updates with an increasing attention to detail. The developer has helped me troubleshoot and they might even incorporate some of my feedback within future updates. 

If you’re hesitant to buy their product, then think of it this way. Apple wants you to subscribe to their iCloud service indefinitely and the developer of this app only wants a one-time contribution from you. That’s it. You’re not renting this product, it is yours to keep. You receive all the future benefits without a monthly/yearly recurring charge to your bank.

Beautiful. Functional. And I love the stats! — This app is not only attractive, but very functional and easy to use. I’m a person who loves reviewing stats.  I look forward to any new feature additions. Good job. Thanx for building. It’s what I need.

Great for Daily Habits — I really like the app, but I didn’t realize until subscribing to pro and adding in lots of habits that it is only set up for daily habits. Being able to schedule habit frequency of twice a week, or schedule for certain days, is a significant element in most habit apps, and it’s really important to me. I don’t want to do 100 habits daily. 

The categories are great… more like tags. Good that you can have multiple, so you can tag as “health” but also tag as “AM Routine” in order to habit stack.

Perfect habit tracking — This is exactly what I’ve been looking for in a habit tracker. Extremely customizable yet simple. There aren’t intrusive blogs or self help notes. It’s just a straight up habit tracking app that is heatmap based. 

Basing the entire app around a heatmap is such a great idea. Every habit has a simple Birds Eye view of its completion history.

Finally the project is owned by a single creator who works hard to put out features. He has a vision for his app and he responds to feature request promptly.

Game changer! — I like tracking with pen + paper but this app is too good not to use! I don’t always carry my journal to track my daily habits, so it is very convenient to have this HabitKit by my side. As a data lover, I enjoy being able to see the total amount of completed habits on set year. Always good to support, especially if the product delivers!!
Visually appealing — Simple & not over complicated! Great balance to easily track habits

Just what I was looking for — I was looking for a streak tracking habit app, and I've found it right here. Minimalistic and visually appealing - lets you focus on things that matter - your habits. Another plus is that developer is very responsive, I've sent him an email with a small suggestion and he replied almost immediately.

Amazing Habit Tracker — This is an awesome app to track your daily habits however the main reason I bought the app, the widgets, are finicky. When a new day happens, I have to open the application for the widgets to show up as incomplete. Also for the checkbox widget it would be so nice to have the ability to “complete” the habit by clicking the small check mark. If both of these were addressed it would be 5 stars easily.

UPDATE: the developer of this app is amazing and actually implemented the only two things about the app I wished were true. 5 stars, amazing app and worth the one time purchase price to unlock widgets.

Great App — This is a great app. Good pricing. Amazing user experience, apart from the lack of multi-device syncing. Everything is customizable and the grid streaking really helps me keep habits. 100% sucess rate with this as opposed to other apps. 

HabitKit is simple and sleek. Must have for anyone using digital planners or habit trackers.

Fantastic app, bad update — The app still works as advertised and is wonderful, but now the widgets on my Home Screen change colors with the time of day and seemingly that can’t be changed. app: 85. Habitica - Gamified Taskmanager - Stay motivated and organized
text:
<33 — I am a data scientist in my 30s and I absolutely love Habitica and use it with my partner. We both have elaborate wardrobes and can be found hollering across the house to come look at eachother's Habitica outfit despite having used it for like 4 years now. There are pay-to-play features but they are not absolute (there are other ways to access those items through the MMO community interaction aspect, it's just harder and less likely) and the basal experience is good enough. I didn't pay for I think the first year; it's $5/mo if you want a consistent in-game monthly income of the higher-tier in-game currency, basically. 

To summarize, you have your own content you can interact with, and other people out in the external Habitica world (you don't walk around on a map, you join groups and essentially engage in an automated tabletop RPG by completing your task list with the computer as the DM). It is 4-seasonal with 4 themed events where you can acquire items that may or may not recur. There is a huge, huge variety of pets you can hatch and evolve (one stage evolution) in any potion color (there are I think 7 basic and an unknown amt of special potions). This is my favorite part. 

The community is very active in improving the codebase and you can create and contribute objects yourself as a pixel artist, though not 100% of submissions are used / you have to get on github and get picked to make them (but it's achievable); there are in-game awards for this kind of contribution. 

I use it for managing my basic self-care tasks and simple errands as I have a chronic illness. Before I was a data scientist I also used it to motivate myself to study coding. There are both boolean valued (check-off) tasks and activities that you can claim an unlimited # of rewards for; you create them. You control this size of the reward you get for the tasks and there is a workaround system to adjust your settings (your gold and mana) if you mess something up or there's a glitch (I've never used this). You cannot alter your amount of the higher-tier currency, potions, etc. and must get a mod to help you if you experience a glitch there (this has happened to me one time, and it was because my internet was flickering in and out rapidly right at the very moment that the reward for the group tabletop-style quest was marked complete; I had other glitches in other softwares due to my computer's behavior so it wasn't their fault but they fixed it within 24hrs). 

Everyone is there in good faith. There are identity-based and task-based groups and a server-wide groupchat for interacting with mods on various pragmatic issues like previously discussed. I forget how, but I don't think Habitica hires mods, I think people become mods through a certain amount of community contribution (might be wrong on this); also anyone can start a group if you have a small amount of the higher-tier currency to put in your group's bank (but you can pull it right back out afterwards, heh). There is a group that goes around taking over and "robbing" the banks of abandoned groups and it has become Habitica-sanctioned, which I love.

Okay, this description is getting out of control. There's a ton more. It's really good. However the gameplay is NOT so spin-offy that it becomes a timewaster in and of itself; doing your tasks drives everything.

app: 16. Atoms - from Atomic Habits - The official Atomic Habits app
text:
I do like the book, but this app has so many design flaws — Hello James,

I've read the book and I really liked it. However, this app is littered with design flaws I have to uninstall it:

1. Paid users can't create more than 6 habits. This is a pretty strange design. A paid user is supposed to create unlimited amount of habits and not get hard locked to only 6 habits. A paid user pays $5/month or $40/year just to create only 6 habits simultaneously? Other similar apps use hard limit to incentivize in-app purchase, not locking them down to a limited version. 
2. Tutorials bombard a new user from the start. No one cares honestly. I just want a habit app that's simple and efficient and it works. It should give me several functions: it can create a habit; it can track a habit; it has a heat map; it can repeat itself in a way I like. Every single tab is pushed with prolonged tutorials on how to use the app properly whereas I just want a simple design that gets the job done. Yes, wisdom, yes, quotes. No one cares. A habit app needs to suffice some basic functions for user to want to use it. I'm on a free trial of this app and I don't even want to use it because I find it just inefficient and does not do the job well. 
3. I understand this is a companion app for the book Atomic Habits, but honestly the app is so littered with unnecessary stuff and hardcoded limits it feels like a waste of time to use it. People use a habit app to record their habits and understand the patterns. Check out some competitor apps you'll see how they design their apps. A habit app is supposed to be simple, efficient, and gets the job done. If these metrics can't even be sufficed, there is no point in 7 tutorials on how to use the app properly and then some. Some tutorials even bugged out on my phone and I had to close them. 
4. I have to input a specific time to a habit? And I also have to hard lock specific days in a week? Absolutely strange design. Let's just say repetition is supposed to be "any 4 days in a week". This is not selectable in the app at all neither can you create the pattern. I also don't understand why a specific time has to be put into place IN ORDER TO create a habit. You can assign a time later plus I don't hard lock a time to a habit I'll do but I do do the habit on the day when time frees out. 

What's great about the app:
1. Finishing a habit feels great. Holding the button and it registers as a completion does feel great. This is a great design. 
2. I do like the quotes and wisdom baked into this app. When you build a habit alongside these wisdom quotes, it does stand out much more than other apps. However, if basic functions can't be sufficed, no amount of wisdom can save a dysfunctional app.

app: 25. Grit - Daily Habit Tracker - Routines & Goals ADHD Planner
text:
Красивое и вкусное — Я перепробовала много трекеров привычек, но Grit зацепил меня сильнее всего, так что в благодарность разработчику я купила lifetime версию.

Приложение очень красивое, им приятно пользоваться, оно не перегружено лишними деталями, мне хочется заходить сюда снова и снова и отмечать свои привычки. На мой взгляд, такие ощущения - это самое важное в трекере привычек, потому что именно они не позволяют забросить приложение через неделю, как это получилось у меня с Habitica - красивым, интересным, но переусложненным трекером, который со временем превратился для меня в работу. Я не хочу сказать, что Habitica плохая, но для такого рассеянного человека с СДВГ как я, разноцветный и вкусненький Grit оказался полезнее и приятнее.

Минусы/пожелания:
1. Хотелось бы увидеть более минималистичный heatmap виджет - без лишних подписей и месяцев. Только название привычки и растянутый на весь виджет heatmap с разноцветными квадратиками, как это сделано в Ripples и Habitkit.
2. В разделе "Статистика" много лишнего и мало полезного. Для мотивации и отслеживания успехов достаточно одного календарика с heatmap и процентом успеха, остальная часть статистики должна быть направлена на понимание того, почему я не выполнила свои привычки. Можно сделать это через трекер настроения (в виде смайликов, на которые можно нажимать каждый день), уровня энергии (в виде батарейки) или кнопки "Почему не получилось" с вариантами ответа, которые бы учитывались в статистике.

My preferred habit tracker! — The UI is so simple, clean, and easy to understand! It is not time consuming to use. After setting up the desired habits and finish them with a tap. I love how I can input my old data into the app. 

The free trial version only allows two habits to be tracked. The one time fee for unlimited trackable habits is so worth it because of the other useful features (dark mode, importing data, reminders, even changing the app color!)   

I love that there are no subscription fees and my data isn’t stored on a server! I don’t rate and buy  apps usually. Buying this app definitely was worth helping out a solo developer!

app: 34. Habit Tracker - Evoday - Daily Streaks Calendar & Goals
text:
Love Habit Tracking! — I love the idea of habit tracking — from exercising (and having separate habits for each excerise I want to do) to eating healthy or going without spending. I’ve tried bullet journaling but it was hard to stay accountable for that, as I much prefer this digital means. On the free version, you can track two habits. I upgraded for $9 so I could get unlimited habits and dark mode (love that feature as well!) The upgrade to premium mode helps support an independent developer as well, so if you really like the app and can spend the money, I would recommend updating to get the unlimited habits and to help support the developer. 

The app interface is clean and easy to navigate. You can make this app work for whatever your needs are! Plus, the reminders are fantastic, as you can set up a certain amount of them per week (3 per week, every day, etc.) I find that extremely helpful to keep track of remembering to log your habits. A+!

app: 34. Habit Tracker - Evoday - Daily Streaks Calendar & Goals
text:
Very good set of features, no subscription — I’ve downloaded like, 20 different ‘habit’ apps and this one has many of the features and design I look for: 
- easy to tally habit as done, and they’re all on one page
- shows week,month, and year overview progress
- no subscription model for premium
- can tally previous days if you forget
- individual reminders and can have multiple of them
- shows streaks 

I’d like some badges/achievements, the ability to track negative habits (eg smoking), and also the ability to track multiple reps per day (eg if you want to keep track of glasses of water you’re drinking or pull-ups etc).

app: 34. Habit Tracker - Evoday - Daily Streaks Calendar & Goals
text: Love this app — This is the best App I’ve been able to find to keep me on track. It helps me keep focused on my daily exercise, my eating habits, like NOT eating things that I love that are bad for me and how many days I can go without eating CANDY. I’m a diabetic and it’s real challenge for me. There are so many things in my life that I  do that I want to stop doing and things that I don’t do that I want to start doing and I keep track of with this app. Needless to say I really like the app and I use it every single day to log my results with just a tap. I’ve been trying for 20 years to lose weight and this app has given me the extra help that I have needed to accomplish my weight loss goal. I finally got under 200 pounds by setting a goal not to eat after 6 PM, not to eat candy and things like that. The simple process of setting a goal and checking off every day showing that you’ve done what you planned really helps. I know that there are other good apps out there to accomplish the same thing but this one really works for me. I like simple, straightforward, uncomplicated easy to use apps that accomplishes my desired results. Oh, I don’t usually do reviews but I like this app so much that I went on and on and on. Sorry! Give it a try, I think you’ll like it!

app: 34. Habit Tracker - Evoday - Daily Streaks Calendar & Goals
text:
Thoughtfully designed, useful app — I have been using this app daily since 9/27 to track both good and bad habits. It's well designed, useful, and my favorite app in the quantified self category. I would only ask for two changes. 

1. The app is designed around positive habits that you want to sustain (e.g. exercise). It does not cater to habits you want to quit. It's subtle, but things like "TO DO," streaks, and minimum goal of 1/wk instead of 0. It's not hard to work around that, but for example I'd rather not see "TO DO" next to bad habits. Just an empty state check box is enough for both good and bad habits. 

2. It would be cool to stack different habits on one graph for comparison. But again, it's not hard to work around by just exporting the data.

text: Excellent tick list tracker — I have been using everyday for over a year, and find it the best tick list tracker I’ve used, and I’ve used a lot of them. It’s easy to use on my iPad, iPhone and Apple Watch.  I also can set tasks for a time period, reach my goal and archive them, which I can then reactivate again another time, which is great for seasonal habits.  The psychology behind the app of building habits to support achieving goals is well founded and works.  If you’re serious about your self-growth, this is a great app.  Since it has a free tier, it is worth giving it a go to see if it works for you.
