text: So far so not sure — I really like the idea and the beautiful look of the app, but the quality and devil is in the details, and the app has some way to go. The first thing I notice is that when I am to make a password, they only ask me to enter it once and I cannot see what I have written. Let’s just hope that I wrote what I thought I did, for the next time I am to login. Then, when I click “+ make new habit”, everything is filled in with my previous habit. I think I am editing my old one, so I click Cancel and try again. The same thing 4-5 times before I finally try to wipe out (there is no x to remove all the previous text either), and enter a new goal specifics on every line. It turns out this was how it should be done. Very non-intuitive. Also, whenever I click to write on a new line, it doesn’t capitalize the First letter which is annoying when you are to look at the habit name every day so I have to go back and Write properly. The UI looks a bit messy with large links to some videos (with some weird names?), other links are small. Basically, I ended up purchasing this to try for a year because I like the concept and the Black Friday deal (which right now is 15 euro, or 1 euro a month as they say - because details are not important and they clearly live in a 15 month year!) but for the price they are charging for this app, I really think they should have a quality control and think more about their user interface. Just follow the standards you see in other apps and you will be well on your way. I hope my monitary contribution will help them become better. And I hope I will become a better self by using this app every day. Win win?

Good, simple, straightforward — I was inspired to try habit formation by a good friend of mine who introduced me to Seinfeld’s X effect. We normally would make giant poster grids with the largest markers we could find at the craft store. The dopamine hit for crossing out a day where a habit was successfully completed was a really satisfying end to the day. Sadly I moved away from my old town, and I haven’t really had much interest in hanging a big poster in my room that I share with my partner.

Everyday fits the bill for this in many ways. It synchronizes really well, it’s much more discreet than the giant posters, and it is VERY easy to document progress. My one, and only, complaint is that it doesn’t have the same dopamine hit as the posters. It’s close with the flash the icons do once they’re tapped, but something more extreme would be greatly appreciated.

text:
Simple app, nice features, very easy to follow through with — You can only make three Habits at a time without paying, and yall have LOST your minds if you think I’m about to pay $99 for such basic functionality. 

That said, I think the limit is beneficial since it kept me from piling expectations onto myself. The process is simple enough that it’s never been overwhelming.

My favorite feature is that you can mark a “null” day, which doesn’t add to OR interrupt a streak. It’s nice for when one of my goals wasn’t possible that day, but I don’t want to let go of my streak. Having this in-between makes it so I never feel the need to lie (which is a quick way to lose motivation).

The visual feedback of marking a completed a habit is nice, especially with the bright colors. Your phone also makes a nice *click* vibration which I like. 
You can also view statistics for how often you follow through with your goals. No ads, and an account isn’t required, which is always a plus.

Overall, very satisfied

app: 46. everyday - Habit Tracker - Daily Routine Checklist
text:
Give this smaller app a chance — I’ve tried a lot of habit trackers, but there is almost always TOO much to fill in that it made me not want to use them. The process of filling everything in felt like it needed to be a habit in itself. 

My ADHD brain gets too distracted; I desperately wanted simplicity. After years, I’ve developed some great habits simply by using timers and reading Atomic Habits, which this app draws some concepts from. Now, I want to visualize this in a simple, easy-understand-visual for novice data folks like my wife or friends. So I turned to this app, (shout out r/dataisbeautiful). This app does just that. With intention and time, I’m excited to see what my visual will look like. Literally 3 click options:

-Did you do it? Tap.
-Did you do some of it? Tap.  Tap.
-Didn’t do it? Tap. Tap. Tap.

Obviously, there are things to fill out. But compared to others, IMO, set up is simple. Reminder options are available. There is even an option for breaking habits! 

Free to use, so I’ve testing with 3 habits and I’m very happy so far. It’s only 1/2, but so far, so good. 

Some improvements for this app, for me, would just be customizable user preferences. Specifically, visuals with fonts. I have unique reading needs so the ability to alter these helps a ton! This would help keep the app accessible for all. TY for your great app.

app: 46. everyday - Habit Tracker - Daily Routine Checklist
text: This app helped me change my life — When I came to realize that habits are one of the fundamental building blocks of achieving success on the vision I have for my life, my next thought was to find the best system for motivating me to do all my goals every day. I really struggle with consistency, but it’s precisely that lack of consistency that is the #1 limiting factor to me achieving my vision for my life. So I went looking for a habit tracking app that really nails the dopamine reward cycle and would help me be the most motivated and therefore consistent with my daily goals. In short: that app is Everyday. I encourage you to try it for free with just three goals, and once you realize like I did how valuable it is, then shell out the few bucks for the premium version. Best ROI on your money of pretty much anything in life I can think of. This app is really robust; the features for how you can set up your habits covers absolutely everything that you could want to track, and they have icons and visuals and the whole main screen is basically a visualization of how consistent you are becoming. And they’re leveraging gamification things to make it more effective. It’s truly the perfect app for this. Can’t recommend it more.

app: 46. everyday - Habit Tracker - Daily Routine Checklist
text:
Good but missing some features I'd like... — I have been searching for a visual tracking app like this for ages. I love the color and how it lets you see so many days/habits at once. There are a couple features I would like though.

1. Is there a way to reorded the way the habits appear in the list? For example, the first habit I made was 'code 10 mins' with a reminder at 1700. But then I made 'yoga 20 mins' with a reminder at 700. I wanted to reorder the habits so they appear in the list chornologically, but was unable to do so. My OCD got the better of me and I ended up deleting the first habit because I couldn't take them being out of order.

2. More color options! Or maybe sets? Like a pastels option. Or a neon options. I would totally splurge a buck 99 for a rain themed color pallete, or something seasonal and dumb.

3. A lower life time purchase price. I usually buy the lifetime option if I know I am going to use an app daily. But 99 dollars is pretty steep, so I ended up going for the yearly subscription. 69.99 and I probably would have paid if I liked the weekly trial (and it had some of the features I mentioned above.) Then you can make extra by releasing fun cosmetic stuff like color palettes, etc. People who are choosing your app are probably choosing it for the ascetics, so I'm sure you could make extra cash that way once you have lifetime subscribers.

All in all hopeful for more updates! This is the only visual habit tracker I've found. I was considering making my own!

text:
Greedy Ludicrous Pricing — If you care about helping the most people possible and doing the most good possible, consider charging what most people will actually pay for a habit app. What’s more important, you making as much money as you can, or you making a bigger impact on the world and uplifting the collective quality of life on earth? Please consider. Thank you for making the app but it is unusable for me at this price range. $100 for a lifetime purchase. For an app that shows a colored tile when I click it? There’s so much more capable software people can buy for $100. Please consider this!

After reading other developer responses it seems the developer does want to help as many people as possible but is having trouble financing their ability to work in coding. 

Is there another solution besides jacking up the price of this 1 app to such high heights?

If you kept the features of this app the same and didn’t work much on it, your work-to-compensation ratio would even out over time even with the app at a lower price point. 

This would free you up to work on other apps/projects. 

If you only want to work on this project and see it as more of a luxury habit-tracking app that caters to richer customers, then alright, I guess I understand. There’s other reasonably priced habit-tracking apps we can use. 

I just have a problem with how many developers are going to subscription model to bleed customers of their money. It’s insane. Almost everything is a subscription now. And it’s not because it’s truly necessary. There’s so much greed now in software. 

There has to be another better way. 

By the way, if 100 different apps & services are trying to charge us the price of a coffee a month, what does that add up to? EVERYONE is trying to do it now.

text: My Most-Used App! — I am now on day seven of using this gorgeous habit tracker, and I love it. The colors are pretty, and I find watching the streaks build very motivating. it syncs flawlessly -- and immediately -- across Chrome, iPhone, and Mac. (I haven't tried it on my watch yet.) I found out it could be set up to open in a fresh tab on Chrome, and it's the best thing ever because I am so frequently reminded of my daily habits and able to easily check them off when I'm ready. The week-long starter email series is very helpful, and the "Learn" tab has a wealth of information on setting and maintaining habits, with lots of scientific background about what works and why. I also had a question for the developer, and she got back to me quickly with a kind, helpful email. In the meantime, I had figured out how to solve the issue, but she mentioned that she would keep playing around with it so that others didn't have the same confusion. As a tip, if you change the colors a lot (as I do, since mine are in rainbow order, so I have to tweak things every time I move/add/archive a habit), the easiest way to do it is via the Chrome extension: hover over the habit name, then click on the color dot to the left and choose a new color.) After all, the beauty is part of the point of the app! (Developer: It would be great if it were this easy to change colors on the Mac app, but this is a good work-around and certainly not a deal-breaker!)

text: You may waste a lot of time with this one. — Free - with in-app purchases. Apple really needs to do something about developers using “Free - with in-app purchases” this way.

I am happy to pay a REASONABLE subscription rate for an app.  Take Deliveries, for example.  Arguably, it's a much more complex app to code and maintain, yet the developer only charges $4.99 PER YEAR.  That is more than fair.  Compare to 1Password.  Everyday is basically the same price!  Absurd!!!  1Password is a far more complex app with a whole development and support team behind it.

All of that said, Everyday is a nice app.  It's intuitive with great use of color, making it both easy to read and visually appealing.  I've had a few email exchanges with the developer and he is friendly and responsive.  I'd pay for the app if it were reasonably priced, but out of principal more than anything else, I refuse to subscribe at these prices.

*Response to the developer:  I agree with what you wrote regarding value.  So let's compare apples to apples.  Awesome Habits is $22.99 for a LIFETIME license.  Habit Tracker (by Davetech Co) is $4.99 for a LIFETIME license.  Each of these apps offers more features than Everyday.  Again, I'm not trying to be a jerk, but $30/year forever is ridiculous.

No clue why the developer suddenly felt the app was worth 3x the price, and moreover, I’m just sad that apps that once went for a one time purchase of $3 to $5 are now trying to charge the same monthly. I blame Apple for that... greedy!

UPDATE: Developer responded below that the price had to go to because the app wasn’t sustainable. That’s the problem with many app developers today. They want to write one app, get customers, then raise the price. They’ve given up on making other apps and adding more value to draw in more customers. Instead, they’re exploiting their one success story and raising prices for the few who are willing to stick around. It’s happening over and over and over. $4 calendar utilities turning into $20 calendar utilities for a “polish” upgrade, turning into $30/year subscriptions - for a calendar utility.

At the end of the day, if you feel like an app that replicates what you can do with a spreadsheet is worth $60/year, go for it. But this sort of price jacking is ruining the App Store, slowly, through attrition. Maybe the balance sheets don’t yet reflect it, but they will.
